To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetron can be frequency locked by a wideband phase modulating signal, and the magnetron phase and power are precisely stable within a wide band of the RF field amplitude in the SRF resonator.
the phase control bandwidth of the magnetron is limited by the phase pulling/pushing time constant.
the frequency pulling/pushing in a magnetron is a transient process.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the magnetron transmitter for the electron collider ring of the MECC facility with the following characteristics: 1) RF power of 1.0 MW; 2) RF frequency of 3.12 GHz; 3) RF pulse duration up to 1 s; 4) RF phase stability of 0.1 deg. rms; 5) RF power stability of 0,1% rms.
the development and application of the magnetron transmitter for the electron collider ring of the ME IC facility.
the development of the high-power magnetron transmitter with wide band phase control for the Electron Collider of the MEIC Project.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnetron is frequency locked and the locking signal is phase modulated, then the magnetron output power is phase modulated with an envelope of the locking signal and the phase of the locking signal.

the frequency pulling/pushing in the frequency locked CW magnetron is described by the equation: The magnetron is frequency locked at the phase pulling/pushing of the RF signal reflected from the cavity, which is proportional to the cavity Q-factor.

the phase controlled frequency locking is possible for a magnetron with the locking signal of 15 dB, the magnetron with a 2 cascade structure is preferable, the magnetron should have an external resonant structure, and a phase modulated locking signal is necessary to obtain the wideband dynamic phase control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that magnetrons can be used as high power CW sources for SRF cavities with a dynamic phase and amplitude control in a wideband.
we have shown the feasibility of a wideband phase and amplitude control in a CW magnetron transmitter for the SRF cavity.
we have shown that the magnetron can be used for compensation of the synchrotron radiation in the electron collider of MEIC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency locked magnetrons are capable to compensate phase deviations in the SRF resonators caused by the beam loading up to ~0.26 deg rms at a steady state.
the magnetron phase control is possible at the locking signal power less than 15 dB.
the phase pulling/pushing is proportional to the derivative of the locking signal phase.
